speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: As for the skills frameworks, they have also been launched for Hotel and Accommodation Services, Early Childhood Care and Education, and Precision Engineering.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Career fairs are also being held to attract Singaporeans, to strengthen our Singaporean Core in these sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: More sectors are in the pipeline, and the relevant career and employment information will be incorporated into our National Jobs Bank as and when it is published.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Will the Minister consider encouraging, particularly, private sector companies, to give forecasts of employment, with these forecasts-giving a factor to be considered when issuing Employment Pass or other work passes?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: If a company makes a forecast very close to the time of recruitment, then Singaporeans may not be able to benefit from it.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Then, the Ministry may be presented with a fait accompli in terms of applications from foreigners for these jobs.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: However, forecasts at the industry level is being done and will continue to be done.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: If I may just give an illustration on how much is being done.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: At the last Parliament Sitting, I shared with this House the skills framework for the hotel sector.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Today, I have brought another two skills frameworks as an illustration.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Page: 11 One is for Early Childhood Care and Education.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In this skills framework, the career paths that are being presented, as we move forward in this sector, are clearly spelt out.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Either you are an educarer, teacher or in a leadership position.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For each of these career paths, there is a detailed description in terms of what are the jobs available, what are the skill requirements and so on.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Therefore, any person who is looking into a career development in the future, in the next three years, can take a look at this and decide for himself/herself whether this is a sector that he/she wants to go into.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: If so, these are the career paths, these are the job positions, as well as the skills that they can pursue.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Here again, you can see that in this skills framework, it is clearly spelt out that anybody can join the sector to pursue two-career tracks.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: One is the engineering and technician track; the other is the management track.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Again, the job positions are well spelt out.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Even the salary range is all in there.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For those who are interested in any particular position, they can go into the detailed write-ups, job by job.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: On the whole, I want to emphasise again that Singapore is one of the very few countries in the world that is putting in so much effort to prepare our workforce and our industries for the future.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Without the Industry Transformation Maps, this skills framework is not possible.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For example, if you look at Precision Engineering, we talk about future manufacturing, which are the four key directions that are happening.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: These are very important because when they know that these are the emerging trends in Precision Engineering, then people will understand what the future openings are.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For example, it is highlighted that robotics and automation are one of the emerging trends.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Digitisation of manufacturing is another emerging trend; so also additive manufacturing, data analysis.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Therefore, I just want to emphasise again and again that we are one of the very few countries in the world that is putting in so much effort to try to visualise the future and try to put in place a skills framework to guide our fellow Singaporeans in their future career selection and development.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I hope that Members of this House can help us to bring out the message to the ground, because all these efforts may not be known enough on the ground.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: But as far as the Ministry of Manpower is concerned, this information, as and when they become available, we will incorporate them into our National Jobs Bank so that workers accessing the Jobs Bank will be able to have this information, decide for themselves which sector to go into, which career path to pursue, what job, what skills are needed and, from there, under SkillsFuture Singapore, they can pursue the skills upgrading in advance of their career change.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It is certainly very encouraging to know that the Government is doing a lot to help the workers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: What is going to help the workers, going ahead, will be that they know that there is a job waiting for them if they have made the required training and they have bothered to upgrade themselves.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Two points of clarification: one, whether the Ministry can consider ways to have more Place and Train programmes with companies; and two, how it is going to work with economic agencies, such as the Economic Development Board, to make sure that the investments that we bring in, the companies will work with the agencies through the Place and Train programmes so that our workers will be job-ready when the investments are here.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Most of our focus today is on Place and Train.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In other words, we try to guide the workers of today and tomorrow in terms of future job openings.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: From there, we put them through training programmes with the support of their employers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In other words, today, you have a job but you are planning ahead for the next three to five years.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, under SkillsFuture, we are encouraging workers to take on the personal responsibility to take on training which may or may not have the support of their employers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, I fully agree with Mr Desmond Choo's point that we have to keep doing more to prepare workers of today for the jobs of tomorrow.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, for those who are already in employment, we try and help them to take on their personal upgrading through personal responsibility under SkillsFuture without having to depend on their employers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Yet, at the same time, for those who are out of employment, the immediate task is to get them a job and train them for the job.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, it is more for Place and Train.
